title: CDC differs from regular sync: per-source schedule, halt markers, paused-is-normal
answers: How does CDC scheduling differ from regular sync?
Why doesn't disabling a CDC schema pause a schedule?
Are paused CDC schedules considered stalled?
body:
- CDC schedule is one per source: `cdc-extraction-{source_id}` (`_get_cdc_extraction_schedule_id`, data_load/service.py). `sync_cdc_extraction_schedule` rebuilds from schemas with sync_type=CDC, should_sync=True, not deleted, source not deleted; interval = min (`cdc_min_interval`). Empty set → schedule DELETED, not paused. So disabling one CDC schema does nothing to the schedule unless callers re-run `sync_cdc_extraction_schedule`.
- Streaming CDC schema (`is_cdc and cdc_mode=="streaming"`): paused per-schema schedule is steady state (CDCExtractionWorkflow owns it). `find_stalled_schemas`/`repair_stalled_schema` (stalled_schedules.py) skip them and any `cdc_halted`; regular schemas with paused schedule and should_sync=True are faults.
- Halt markers live in `sync_type_config`: `cdc_broken` (slot/publication gone) and `cdc_extraction_paused` (non-retryable error, slot intact). `cdc_halted` = either; `sync_halted` = not should_sync or cdc_halted.
- `mark_cdc_broken` (cdc/broken.py): sets marker + status=FAILED + latest_error on all active CDC schemas, source status=ERROR, pauses schedule via `pause_cdc_extraction_schedule`; under source row lock, uses `update_sync_type_config_keys` to avoid clobbering PATCHes.
- Halted states are absorbing: job status update (external_data_source/jobs.py) must not repaint a halted schema healthy when a loader finishes late.
- Repair (cdc/repair.py) covers all CDC schemas including should_sync=False ones, since the new slot can't replay lost data.
applies: CDC sources (sync_type=CDC) only; regular schemas use per-schema schedules.
